pr_title: Core: add location global for non-browsers, fix #1788
pr_body:
This is a simple fix that will also prevent future problems with this.
Of course, it would be nice to add a test, but I think it's a bit beyond the scope at the moment.
Poke #1788.
pr_comments:
Normally I'd say we do want a test here but once #1722 is resolved we'll have basic Node testing covered (see https://github.com/jquery/jquery/commit/e1303a38197b36297ce6190ad318fc9e73876298) so I think we don't need anything tested separately here.
Can you sign the [CLA](http://contribute.jquery.org/CLA/)?
If the PR doesn't come with tests or other fixes, it's probably easier for us to do it as part of #1788 and you won't  need to sign the CLA. Clearly we can make the one-line edit, that's the easy part. It may be possible to get even better regression-proofness with some JSHint options. Again that would be the research/work that makes the PR worthwhile.
@dmethvin Since we're just after a release and we're not going to release 2.1.3 in a moment you're right that it doesn't buy us much. Let's close it then.

issue_context.title: 2.1.2-pre, ajax.js: environments that don't have 'location' variable will break
issue_context.body:
Originally reported by brianblocker at: http://bugs.jquery.com/ticket/15210

It appears that the change which removes the "IE workaround" on ajax.js now breaks environments that do not have window.location. To be specific:

(from  https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/master/src/ajax.js#L44) ajaxLocation = location.href,

When I try to run automated tests using jasmine-node, location is undefined (because there is no "browser" sorta), and therefore the test breaks. Using the previous version (2.1.1-pre) works fine, but it appears that the change introduced in 2.1.2-pre now breaks the environment.

Issue reported for jQuery 2.1.1
